<INSTRUCTIONS>
# Codex Bridge for openvela AI Skills

This repository carries a Claude-oriented skill pack under `.claude/`. Codex
does not auto-load that directory, so use this file as the project bridge.

## General Workflow

- For openvela, NuttX, ESP32-S3, audio, build, driver, size, memory, Kconfig,
  PR, or contest-log tasks, first check whether a matching skill exists in
  `.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`.
- When a matching skill is relevant, read its `SKILL.md` completely before
  acting. If that file points to specific `references/` or `scripts/`, load
  only the files needed for the current task.
- Treat `.claude/skills` as shared source material. Do not rewrite or move it
  unless the user explicitly asks.
- Claude-specific files such as `.claude/settings.local.json`,
  `.claude/commands/`, and `.claude/agents/*.agent.md` are not Codex runtime
  configuration. They may be read as workflow documentation, but Codex still
  follows its own sandbox, approval, and tool rules.
- Prefer repo-local scripts from the selected skill when they fit the task, but
  inspect them before running commands that may modify files, access the
  network, or depend on external credentials.
- Keep user-facing discussion in Chinese unless the user asks otherwise.
  Code comments, commit messages, and upstream-facing patches should follow
  the surrounding project style.

## Skill Routing

Use these `.claude` skills as the first stop for matching work:

- `openvela-build`: building firmware, running emulator, menuconfig guidance,
  build failures.
- `openvela-quickstart`: first-time environment setup, repo init/sync,
  dependency checks, source selection.
- `nuttx-driver-development`: creating or updating NuttX/openvela drivers,
  board registration, Kconfig/build integration, subsystem patterns.
- `driver-code-reviewer`: driver review requests. Default to review-only; do
  not modify code unless the user asks for fixes.
- `pcm-audio`: PCM capture/playback quality analysis, clipping, silence,
  clicks, noise floor, periodic distortion, audio test generation.
- `memdump`: NuttX heap memdump analysis, leak detection, memory comparison.
- `codesize`: ELF/map/archive size analysis and version size comparison.
- `kconfig-tweak`: command-line `.config` edits and config state queries.
- `contest-log-collector`: AI contest session/log collection, export,
  validation, and log packaging.
- `submit-pr`: openvela community PR workflow. Use only after confirming
  credentials, remotes, branch names, and user intent.
- `tmux` or `executor`: persistent interactive processes. Use Codex-native
  terminal sessions when sufficient; only follow these skills when their
  specific behavior is needed.
- `skill-creator`: creating or updating skill documentation.

## Driver Workflow Agent

`.claude/agents/driver-workflow.agent.md` is a Claude agent definition, not a
Codex agent. When the user asks for the full driver workflow, read it as a
process guide, then execute the steps with Codex tools. Preserve its mandatory
checkpoints when they matter, especially requirement confirmation before code
generation.

## Contest Audio Project Notes

For work under `contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/app/audio_event/`, the most
likely useful skills are:

- `pcm-audio` for microphone capture and audio-quality debugging.
- `openvela-build` for firmware build and flash-test preparation.
- `contest-log-collector` when the user asks to export, collect, or package AI
  coding logs for the contest.

Before changing audio capture, board bring-up, or model-calibration docs, read
the local source/docs involved in the request and keep edits scoped to the
contest project.

</INSTRUCTIONS>

### Architecture & Module Structure

cAGENT is a **C Agent inference core library** for embedded and cross-device platforms (openvela/NuttX, ESP-IDF, STM32/FreeRTOS, bare-metal, POSIX). It is architectured as a layered library with the following modules:

#### Module Dependency Graph (from code)

```
Application / Demo
    |  register tools, skills, providers, policy
    v
Public API: include/agent.h + include/cagent/*.h (12 headers)
    |
    +-- Core (src/core/) -- Lifecycle, ReAct loop, event dispatch, context builder
    |     includes agent_internal.h which aggregates:
    |       memory/memory_internal.h
    |       skills/skills_internal.h
    |       tools/tools_internal.h
    |
    +-- LLM (src/llm/) -- Model abstraction layer
    |     model.c       -> agent_model_create/destroy/complete/cancel (facade)
    |     model_openai.c -> OpenAI-compatible non-streaming provider (complete implementation)
    |     model_mock.c   -> Scripted mock model for testing
    |     llm_parse.c    -> Response text parser (final| and tool| pipe formats)
    |     llm_router.c   -> Placeholder stub for optional model router
    |
    +-- Tools (src/tools/) -- Registry, schema builder, guarded execution
    |     tool_registry.c -> agent_register_tool/unregister/set_enabled, lookup
    |     tool_schema.c   -> Builds OpenAI-compatible tools JSON array, cached
    |     tool_guard.c    -> Policy check + execute with timeout/size guards
    |
    +-- Skills (src/skills/) -- Context resources (not executable code)
    |     skill_registry.c -> register/unregister, context build for enabled skills
    |
    +-- Memory (src/memory/) -- Session management, snapshot/restore
    |     session_mgr.c   -> Bounded in-memory session with turn-based eviction

    |
    +-- Runtime (src/runtime/) -- Platform abstraction layer
          runtime.c          -> POSIX fallback + fill_platform dispatch
          runtime_openvela.c -> openvela/NuttX adapter (pthread, mbedTLS HTTPS)
          runtime_espidf.c   -> ESP-IDF/FreeRTOS adapter (semaphores, esp_timer)
          runtime_stm32.c    -> STM32 adapter (FreeRTOS + bare-metal profiles)
```

#### Key Architectural Invariants (from docs and code)

1. **Core never includes platform headers** -- all platform access goes through `agent_runtime_t` callbacks.
2. **Internal headers (`src/**/`) are never exposed to applications** -- only `include/agent.h` and `include/cagent/*.h` are public.
3. **All embedded resources have compile-time upper bounds** -- CAGENT_MAX_TOOLS, CAGENT_MAX_SESSIONS, etc. Support three-tier mapping: direct define > Kconfig CONFIG_* > built-in default.
4. **Tools are the only executable extension point** -- Skills are context-only, they inject into system prompt but don't run code.
5. **Model provider is replaceable** via `agent_model_ops_t` vtable -- core does not bind to any cloud vendor.
6. **Sync-first** -- `agent_run()` is the MVP. Step-based async (agent_begin/step/cancel) is deferred.

#### ReAct Loop Flow (from `agent_loop.c`)

```
agent_run() -> validate -> mutex lock -> set busy -> emit RUN_START
  -> agent_loop_run()
    -> session add user message
    -> allocate request arena
    -> for iter < max_steps:
      -> check cancel_requested / deadline
      -> build context (system_prompt + providers + skills) via context_builder.c
      -> build tool schema JSON via tool_schema.c (cached, dirty-tracked)
      -> build session messages JSON via session_mgr.c
      -> model.complete() via model.c facade -> provider-specific (OpenAI/mock)
      -> parse response
      -> if final content: session add assistant, emit FINAL, return AGENT_OK
      -> if tool_calls:
        -> session add assistant tool_calls
        -> for each tool_call: registry lookup -> policy check -> guard check -> execute -> session add tool result
        -> continue
    -> return AGENT_ERROR_LIMIT
  -> update stats
  -> emit RUN_DONE / CANCELLED / TIMEOUT / ERROR
  -> clear busy, mutex unlock
```

# NuttX Driver Development

Follow the full driver lifecycle in order. Keep edits small and testable.

> [!TIP] This skill can be used standalone or via the `driver-workflow` agent (`agents/driver-workflow.agent.md`) for end-to-end driver development with automated reference matching, requirements generation, and PR submission.

## Preparation

### 1) Clarify scope and expectations

- Identify the NuttX driver subsystem (sensor, serial, timer, analog, etc.).
- Confirm target bus (I2C, SPI, 1-Wire, etc.) and required hardware properties.
- Clarify the NuttX source tree location. The driver code lives under `nuttx/drivers/`.

### 2) Find reference drivers

> [!NOTE] Two types of reference drivers serve different purposes
>
> - **骨架参考（NuttX API 模式）**: 优先使用 NuttX in-tree 同类驱动作为代码骨架，确保符合 NuttX 的 upper-half/lower-half 架构和 VFS 集成方式
> - **芯片参考（寄存器/时序验证）**: 优先使用 Linux/Zephyr 同芯片驱动，用于交叉验证 datasheet 的寄存器定义、初始化序列、SPI 帧格式等芯片专属知识
>
> When used standalone: 手动搜索两类参考驱动
> When used with `driver-workflow` agent: Step A.2 自动完成两条线的并行搜索

Always look at the in-tree NuttX drivers before doing any work. There might already be a driver that (best scenario at the top):

1. Is exactly the same part as the one you are working on
2. Targets a very similar part from the same vendor (e.g., BMP280 vs BME680)
3. Is the same device subsystem as yours (e.g., another I2C sensor)

If a reference driver is found, use it as a **skeleton template**:

1. Copy the source file structure (function signatures, bus access pattern, registration flow, file layout)
2. Replace all device-specific content: register definitions, chip ID values, vendor/chip names, init sequences, calibration logic
3. After generating code, grep for the original chip name — zero matches required
4. **Do NOT copy register addresses or chip-specific constants** — these must come from the target device's datasheet

Re-use these files/folders whenever possible:
- Header files in `include/nuttx/sensors/`, `include/nuttx/i2c/`, etc.
- Existing board-level registration patterns in `boards/`

If no suitable reference driver exists:

1. Use the dispatch table below to load the subsystem-specific pattern reference
2. Use the most similar subsystem's reference driver as template (e.g., use accelerometer driver as template for gyro)
3. Follow the architectural pattern (uORB vs chardev) strictly from the loaded reference
4. For 🔲 Planned subsystems, use `chardev_pattern.md` (Production-Quality Skeleton section) as the starting point

Here are the relevant folders to search for examples:

```
nuttx/
├── drivers/          # Device-specific driver sources. Search here first
│   ├── sensors/      # Sensor drivers (I2C/SPI/1-Wire)
│   ├── serial/       # UART/serial drivers
│   ├── i2c/          # I2C bus framework
│   ├── spi/          # SPI bus framework
│   ├── timers/       # Timer/watchdog/RTC drivers

├── include/nuttx/    # Public header files for driver APIs

├── boards/           # Board-specific initialization & driver registration
└── arch/             # Architecture-specific lower-half bus implementations
```

Use `references/nuttx_nav_search.md` for driver examples and navigating the NuttX repo.

#### Pattern A: Upper-Half / Lower-Half — Preferred for Subsystem Drivers

Most NuttX driver subsystems (sensors, timers, serial, audio, etc.) use an upper-half/lower-half split. The upper-half provides the VFS interface and common logic; you only implement the lower-half callbacks.

```
Application
    │  open/read/write/ioctl/poll
    ▼
  VFS (/dev/...)
    │
    ▼
  Upper-half (provided by NuttX)  ← Generic, handles VFS + common logic
    │  subsystem-specific callbacks
    ▼
  Lower-half (your driver)  ← You implement these
    │
    ▼
  Bus API (I2C_TRANSFER / SPI_*)
```

**When to use**: Always prefer this when the subsystem provides an upper-half framework. Load the corresponding reference document from the dispatch table for implementation details.

#### Pattern B: Standalone Character Device Driver

The simplest pattern. The driver directly implements `struct file_operations` and registers with `register_driver()`.

```
Application
    │  open/read/write/ioctl/close
    ▼
  VFS (/dev/mydevN)
    │
    ▼
  file_operations  ← Your driver implements these
    │
    ▼
  Bus API (I2C_TRANSFER / SPI_LOCK+SPI_SELECT+SPI_RECVBLOCK)
```

**When to use**: Only when the device doesn't fit any existing subsystem, or when existing in-tree drivers for the same device class already use this pattern (e.g., some vibrator or custom peripheral drivers).

See `references/chardev_pattern.md` for standalone character device implementation details.

### 4) Layout the driver files

Define the files that will be created/modified. The exact layout depends on the subsystem — refer to the loaded reference document for subsystem-specific examples.

General layout:

```
nuttx/
├── drivers/<subsystem>/
│   ├── mydevice.c            # Driver implementation
│   ├── Make.defs             # Add CSRCS += mydevice.c
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt        # Add list(APPEND SRCS mydevice.c)
│   └── Kconfig               # Add CONFIG_<SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE entry
├── include/nuttx/<subsystem>/
│   └── mydevice.h            # Public header: register function prototype
└── boards/<arch>/<chip>/<board>/src/
    └── <board>_mydevice.c    # Board-level init: get bus, call register
```

## Code Review

6-dimension review covering initialization, power management, API usage,
critical section & ISR, runtime environment, and coding style.

### Review Process

1. Read `.c`, `.h`, Kconfig, Make.defs, CMakeLists.txt. Identify driver pattern
   (uORB sensor / standalone chardev / RPMsg / other upper-half/lower-half).
2. Run 6-dimension checklist — mark each item PASS / WARN / FAIL.
   See [driver_review_checklist.md](references/driver_review_checklist.md).
3. Run nxstyle check: `nuttx/tools/checkpatch.sh -f <file.c>` (skip if unavailable).
4. Generate structured report (template in checklist reference).
5. For each FAIL/WARN: provide line number + fix snippet + rule reference.

### Review Rules

- FAIL items must be fixed before submission. Auto-fix and re-check until zero FAIL.
- WARN items are listed for user decision.
- If more than 5 issues found on file save, recommend running full review.

source "$BINDIR/arch/risc-v/src/board/Kconfig"

config ARCH_BOARD_ESP32P4_FUNCTION_EV_BOARD
	bool
	default y

config ESP32P4_FUNCTION_EV_BOARD_DSI_FRAMEBUFFER
	bool "Register the P4X MIPI-DSI framebuffer"
	depends on ESPRESSIF_SPIRAM_USER_HEAP
	depends on !LVX_USE_DEMO_CONTEST2026_031_DSI_PROBE
	select ESPRESSIF_MIPI_DSI
	select ESPRESSIF_MIPI_DSI_VIDEO
	select ESPRESSIF_MIPI_DSI_VIDEO_DMA
	select ESPRESSIF_MIPI_DSI_DPI_PANEL
	select VIDEO_FB
	select FB_UPDATE
	default n
	help
		Initialize the EK79007 1024x600 MIPI-DSI panel during board
		bring-up and expose its single RGB565 PSRAM scanout buffer as
		/dev/fb0.  FBIO_UPDATE performs the cache clean required before
		GDMA reads CPU-rendered pixels.

		This is mutually exclusive with the staged dsi_probe demo because
		both own the one P4 DSI Host and EK79007 panel lifecycle.

config ESP32P4_FUNCTION_EV_BOARD_GT911
	bool "Initialize GT911 touchscreen"
	depends on ESPRESSIF_I2C0 && ESPRESSIF_I2C0_MASTER_MODE
	select INPUT
	select INPUT_GT911
	default n
	help
		Register the P4X LCD adapter's Goodix GT911 capacitive touch
		controller as /dev/input0.  The reference board routes the shared
		I2C bus to GPIO8 (SCL) and GPIO7 (SDA), but does not route the
		controller reset or interrupt signals to the ESP32-P4.  The first
		board integration therefore uses a 20 ms polling worker.

if ESP32P4_FUNCTION_EV_BOARD_GT911

config ESP32P4_FUNCTION_EV_BOARD_GT911_MAX_POINTS
	int "GT911 touch points exposed to applications"
	range 1 5
	default 1
	---help---
		Number of simultaneous GT911 contacts exported through /dev/input0.
		Keep the P4X default at one point while using the upstream LVGL NuttX
		adapter: it reads fixed-size samples based on TSIOC_GETMAXPOINTS,
		whereas GT911 produces variable-size frames.  The Smart Home UI uses
		single-touch interactions only.  Raising this value requires a
		variable-length LVGL touchscreen adapter.

endif # ESP32P4_FUNCTION_EV_BOARD_GT911

endif # ARCH_BOARD_CUSTOM

能加，但当前仓库离“摄像头可用”还差采集驱动和板级接线这一步；识别方案建议分层，不要一开始就上本地 YOLO。

目前的事实是：

- `contest_board` 是明确的占位骨架，连启动初始化都没有，因此无法判断相机型号或引脚。[README](/home/arongw/openvela/contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/board/contest_board/README.md:1)
- ESP32-P4 的芯片代码能看到 CSI/LCD_CAM 中断和相机 GPIO 信号定义，但仓库没有现成的摄像头采集驱动或板级注册代码。
- `esp32p4-function-ev-board` 现有工作重点是 DSI 屏幕和 GT911 触摸，并启用了 PSRAM；这对帧缓存/模型运行是好基础，但不等于摄像头已接通。[defconfig](/home/arongw/openvela/contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/board/esp32p4/esp32p4-function-ev-board/configs/smart_home/defconfig:30)

我建议的路线是：

```text
摄像头采集 → JPEG 图像
             ├─ 本地检测（快、私密、确定性强）
             └─ 多模态 API（语义理解强）
                    ↓
             结构化识别结果 → cAGENT 工具结果 → 对话/UI/设备控制
```

首选方案是“摄像头 + 多模态 API”，因为最适合先做出可演示的智能家居能力：例如“看看桌上有什么”“识别垃圾分类”“门口是否有人/包裹”“帮我描述当前画面”。触发方式应是用户点按或语音指令后抓一帧 JPEG 上传，**不要持续上传视频流**。

cAGENT 目前不能直接把图片作为请求输入：`agent_request_t` 只有文本 `input` 字段，[types.h](/home/arongw/openvela/contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/packages/cAGENT/include/cagent/types.h:254)；OpenAI-compatible provider 也只构造文本消息。[model_openai.c](/home/arongw/openvela/contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/packages/cAGENT/src/llm/model_openai.c:223)  
因此更稳的接入方式是新增 `analyze_latest_image` 工具：工具内部拿 JPEG 调用视觉 API，只把精简 JSON 结果返回给 cAGENT，比如 `{"objects":["cup","phone"],"person":true}`。这样不会把大体积 Base64 图片塞进 agent 的上下文和工具输出缓冲。

本地 YOLO 也可以做，但应定位为第二阶段：

- 本地对象检测：适合“有人/无人”“是否检测到杯子、门、宠物”等固定类别；模型要 INT8、小输入分辨率、低帧率触发式运行。
- 本地姿态检测：比目标检测更重。若目标是“跌倒/挥手/抬手”，先做单人、低分辨率、关键点或动作分类；不建议一开始追求多人 17 点实时姿态。
- 仓库已经拉取 TFLite Micro 依赖，具备做本地轻量模型的基础。[openvela.xml](/home/arongw/openvela/contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/openvela.xml:24) 但当前没有 YOLO/姿态模型、图像预处理或推理流水线，仍需从零集成和实机测内存、延迟。

如果这是比赛项目，我会建议优先级：

1. 先确认实际硬件：ESP32-P4 还是 ESP32-S3、相机模块型号、接口是 DVP/并口、MIPI-CSI 还是 USB-UVC，以及可用 PSRAM。
2. 完成“拍一张 JPEG 并显示/保存”的最小链路。
3. 接入一次一图的多模态 API，做可解释的视觉问答。
4. 再根据展示需求补一个本地小模型，例如“人形检测”或“挥手/跌倒动作识别”。

我个人会选“云端多模态 + 本地简单人形/运动触发”的混合方案：本地负责快速、隐私友好的触发；云端只在需要语义理解时分析单帧。对于开锁、报警等动作，视觉模型结果只能作为建议，仍应通过 cAGENT 的策略和二次确认。

在当前 openvela Smart Home 中，**没有“外部事件触发 agent”的现成总线**；现有 agent 主要由 UI、App Bridge 或网关提交文本任务，再在 worker 线程中执行。

关键点是：跌倒判定不能交给 Agent/大模型来决定，也不能让摄像头采集线程直接调用 `agent_run()`。

```text
摄像头/姿态模型
  → 连续帧确认、去重
  → 跌倒事件状态机
  → 本地紧急动作（立即）
  → 异步通知 Agent（辅助处置）
```

建议设计成下面的状态机：

```text
NORMAL
  → SUSPECTED      单帧候选，不能报警
  → CONFIRMED      连续多帧满足阈值，或视觉二次确认
  → WAIT_ACK       本地语音/屏幕询问“您还好吗？”
  → ESCALATED      超时未响应，通知家属/平台
  → RESOLVED       用户取消、人工确认或超时结束
```

触发条件不宜只看“人体横躺”。可以组合：

- 姿态模型连续 N 帧判为跌倒，置信度超过阈值；
- 人体框的高度宽度比快速改变；
- 人体中心短时间明显下移；
- 随后静止一段时间；
- 可选：IMU 的冲击事件做交叉验证；
- 对同一跟踪目标设置冷却时间，避免一秒内反复触发。

其中 `CONFIRMED` 后要立刻执行确定性的本地动作，例如开灯、蜂鸣器、保存事件时间戳、弹出确认页。这些不依赖网络，也不等 Agent 回复。然后才异步提交给 Agent：

```text
系统安全事件：检测到疑似跌倒。
event_id=fall-...
time=...
confidence=0.93
location=living_room
user_ack=false

请生成简短语音询问，并调用“通知联系人”工具；
禁止自行执行开锁、拨打急救电话等高风险动作。
```

在这个项目里，接入点建议是新增 `fall_event_service`，而不是复用检测线程直接调 agent：

- `smart_home_agent_run()` 最终会同步调用 `agent_run()`。[smart_home_agent.c](/home/arongw/openvela/contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/demos/smart_home/src/agent/smart_home_agent.c:757)
- cAGENT 的 `agent_run()` 不可重入；同时聊天与跌倒事件会竞争同一个 agent。
- 现有 [`smart_home_agent_run_service.c`](/home/arongw/openvela/contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/demos/smart_home/src/agent/smart_home_agent_run_service.c:23) 虽然已有 worker + 信号量，但它只能存一条待执行消息，忙时直接返回 `AGENT_ERROR_BUSY`，不适合紧急事件。

所以应建一个独立的、可去重的“安全事件队列”：

```text
fall_detector callback
  → fall_event_manager_confirm()
      ├─ emergency_local_action()       必达，不等网络
      ├─ notify_ui / notify_remote()    必达或重试
      └─ enqueue_agent_summary()        最佳努力，不阻塞
```

Agent 只负责两类事：

1. 把结构化事件转成自然语言播报、给家属的简报；
2. 在策略允许范围内调用通知、开灯、调取事件快照等工具。

它不应负责“是否跌倒”的最终判断，也不应成为紧急处置的唯一通路。现有 cAGENT 的 `agent_event_cb` 只是 Agent 自己运行过程的通知，不是向 Agent 注入跌倒事件的接口；并且回调要求快速返回。[event.h](/home/arongw/openvela/contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/packages/cAGENT/include/cagent/event.h:1)

我还会做两项隔离：

- 为安全事件用独立 session，例如 `safety`，避免“跌倒告警”混入用户普通聊天历史；当前 `smart_home_agent_run()` 固定使用一个会话，需要小幅扩展接口。
- 给“通知联系人/外呼/开门”单独加策略。当前 `REQUIRE_CONFIRM` 在 cAGENT MVP 中等同拒绝，因此高风险动作应由跌倒状态机按明确规则执行，而非期待 Agent 发起确认。[policy.h](/home/arongw/openvela/contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/packages/cAGENT/include/cagent/policy.h:1)

若要做比赛 Demo，我会先实现“本地连续帧确认 → 屏幕告警与语音询问 → 10 秒未确认则调用 Agent 生成并发送家属通知”的闭环。你希望跌倒识别依赖摄像头、IMU，还是两者融合？

- 已绑定的模型连接配置、工具、技能、策略；
- 会话历史和统计信息；
- Agent 的运行时对象。

每次 `agent_run()` 新建/重置的是本轮推理的临时上下文、HTTP 请求、模型调用和工具执行流程。

```text
       ├─ 组装 messages JSON
       └─ agent_model_complete()
             ↓
           OpenAI-compatible HTTP POST
             ↓
           解析文本或 tool_calls
             ↓
       若有 tool_calls：执行工具后再请求 LLM
       若是最终文本：写入 session 并返回
```

具体过程如下。

1. Smart Home 把输入包装成 `agent_request_t`

当前固定使用 `SMART_HOME_SESSION_ID`，并把用户输入赋给 `request.input`，然后调用 `agent_run()`。[smart_home_agent.c](/home/arongw/openvela/contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/demos/smart_home/src/agent/smart_home_agent.c:757)

2. `agent_run()` 做运行控制

它检查参数、加锁防止并发运行、设置本轮 deadline，并进入 `agent_loop_run()`。[agent_core.c](/home/arongw/openvela/contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/packages/cAGENT/src/core/agent_core.c:149)

3. 写入会话并构造发送给 LLM 的三部分数据

当前输入先作为 `user` message 写入 session。随后每个 ReAct step 构造：

- `context`：system prompt + 已注册的上下文提供器 + skills；
- `tools_json`：已注册工具的 OpenAI tool schema；
- `messages_json`：本 session 的历史消息，包含本轮用户输入、此前 assistant 回复和工具结果。

对应代码在 [`agent_loop.c`](/home/arongw/openvela/contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/packages/cAGENT/src/core/agent_loop.c:237) 和 [`context_builder.c`](/home/arongw/openvela/contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/packages/cAGENT/src/core/context_builder.c:1)。

会话太长时，会淘汰最早的完整对话轮次后重试，而非无边界增长。

4. 通过 provider 调用 LLM

`agent_model_complete()` 是一次 vtable 分发；目前 Smart Home 初始化时绑定的是 `agent_model_openai_create()` 创建的 provider。

OpenAI provider 将上述数据拼成类似请求：

```json
{
  "model": "你的模型名",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "system prompt + 设备状态 + skills"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "之前的用户消息"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "之前的回复"},
    {"role": "tool", "content": "{\"ok\":true}"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "当前输入"}
  ],
  "tools": [ ...工具 schema... ],
  "tool_choice": "auto",
  "max_tokens": 512
}
```

拼装逻辑在 [`model_openai.c`](/home/arongw/openvela/contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/packages/cAGENT/src/llm/model_openai.c:216)，之后通过 runtime 的 `http_post` 发送到 `host + path + port`，并带 `Authorization: Bearer <API key>`。[model_openai.c](/home/arongw/openvela/contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/packages/cAGENT/src/llm/model_openai.c:608)

5. LLM 返回后的两条路径

- 返回普通 `content`：保存为 assistant message，复制到 `agent_response.output`，本次 `agent_run()` 结束。
- 返回 `tool_calls`：cAGENT 先保存 tool call，再依次执行本地工具，工具结果作为 `tool` message 写回 session，然后进入下一轮 LLM 请求。

因此一次 `agent_run()` 可能对应：

```text
用户输入 → LLM → 最终回复
```

也可能是：

```text
用户输入 → LLM → 工具调用 → 工具结果 → LLM → 最终回复
```

甚至多个工具循环，直到拿到最终文本或达到 `max_steps`。工具循环实现见 [`agent_loop.c`](/home/arongw/openvela/contest2026_031_niudanxianqianchong/packages/cAGENT/src/core/agent_loop.c:366)。

对跌倒事件而言，可以把结构化事实转成一条 system-style 的事件文本交给一个独立 `safety` session。但“报警、开灯、保留证据”等首要动作仍应由本地事件状态机先完成；LLM 调用是后续解释、通知编排和交互确认。
